fact: The central pearl of Orion's Belt — a blazing blue supergiant seen across vast distance.
bio: Alnilam (Epsilon Orionis) is a blue supergiant more than a thousand light-years away, the middle and most distant of the three stars of Orion's Belt. Its enormous true luminosity lets it hold its own in the Belt despite that gulf of space.
cultural: The name is Arabic for 'the string of pearls'. The three Belt stars are among the most universally recognised in the sky, used as a pointer to Sirius and Aldebaran and woven into star-lore worldwide.
